beats.narration_text: What is it? Walker Tank is a 2D top-down tank game. You drive Yoon-chee Zee through a ruined brick battlefield, against three enemy tanks. This is the game as it exists today, recorded at the A7 tag, and driven by a script, not by a player.

beats.narration_text: When the project is done, it will be a Windows desktop build of one finished level: a title screen, the battle, and a win or lose screen, plus a test report that a stranger can rerun with one command. None of that exists yet.

beats.narration_text: Why would anyone care? I played a 2D browser tank game on seven K seven K, called Chwan-min Tahn-kuh Dah-jahn. As I remember it, cover could not be destroyed, firing had no effect, and a destroyed tank did not smoke. This is drawn from my memory, with no art from that game.

beats.narration_text: Who opens it? A hiring manager or a lead engineer, hiring a gameplay programmer. In the first sixty seconds, they will unzip the build, double-click the exe, see the title screen with the controls on it, press start, and be driving within a minute, without reading anything.

beats.narration_text: What does it prove? Shaders, from A5. Particles, the cover burst and the damage smoke, from A6. Animation clips with pinned state tests, from A7. These tests passed again today, headless. And profiling: plus zero point zero two three and plus zero point zero seven seven milliseconds of GPU time, measured in A6 on an NVIDIA RTX thirty-sixty Laptop GPU.

beats.narration_text: What could make it fail? The game has never been exported. Every test so far ran in the editor or headless, on one machine with an RTX thirty-sixty. Forward plus needs a GPU that supports Vulkan or Direct-3D twelve, so the build may fail or look wrong on a reviewer's laptop with integrated graphics.
beats.display_text: What could make it fail? The game has never been exported. Every test so far ran in the editor or headless, on one machine with an RTX 3060. Forward+ needs a GPU that supports Vulkan or Direct3D 12, so the build may fail or look wrong on a reviewer's laptop with integrated graphics.

beats.narration_text: So I will export in the first week, and run the build on a second machine. If it fails, I'll switch to the Compatibility renderer, recheck each shader and particle effect, and log what changed. I'm not choosing a web export, because it runs only on Compatibility.

shot.visual_intent: A switch flips from Forward+ to Compatibility; effect tiles get checks one by one beside a log page; a web tile is crossed out.

beats.narration_text: Why this project? It's a mix of showing off and learning. Shaders, particles, animation, profiling and testing are shown, with evidence, at tags A5, A6 and A7. Exporting, running on a machine I don't control, and finishing a game from title screen to end screen are new to me. A recruiter can't judge parts. They can judge a finished level.

shot.visual_intent: Left shelf: five evidence blocks tagged a5/a6/a7 (shown). Right: three open outlines (new to me), labelled constructed. The parts slide together into one finished-level box.

beats.narration_text: So, today: a battlefield where cover breaks, Yoon-chee Zee flashes red, and damage smokes. What will exist: one finished level, in a Windows build, with a test report you can rerun. That's my final project. Thanks for watching.
